[Perf] DSv4.1: Cache image preprocessing across requests

## Motivation

Multi-turn agents resend every earlier image on each turn, and the DeepSeek-V4.1 processor decodes and patchifies all of them again in the tokenizer process. The output only depends on the image bytes and the patchify backend, so it can be cached. Kimi-K3, Qwen-VL and Muse Spark already do this through `MediaArtifactCacheMixin`. This PR wires DeepSeek-V4.1 into it.

## Modifications

- `DeepseekV41ImageProcessor` now uses `MediaArtifactCacheMixin`, following the Kimi-K3 and Muse adapters.
  - `DeepseekV41ImagePreprocessArtifact` stores the CPU patchify output: `feature`, `n_vit_h`, `n_vit_w`, `token_count`.
  - `prepare_artifact_batch` patchifies cache misses. `_compose_request` places artifacts into the current prompt's token IDs.
  - The feature hash comes from the artifact key (image bytes plus processor fingerprint, which includes the patchify backend), as in Muse. A miss no longer hashes the patch tensor.
  - Patchify runs on `io_executor`, as in Muse, so it stays off the tokenizer event loop when no processor worker pool is configured.
- The cache is on by default at 256 MiB (`auto_mm_preprocess_cache_size_mb`), matching Kimi-K3 and Muse. `--mm-preprocess-cache-size-mb` resizes it and `0` turns it off.
- The GPU preprocessing backend, preprocessed inputs and cache-off requests keep the existing path. It is unchanged except for sharing the placeholder count check.
- New CPU unit tests in `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_deepseek_v41_processor.py`:
  - Cached and uncached paths produce the same `input_ids`, offsets, `n_vit_h/w` and patches for two images of different sizes.
  - A repeated image skips patchify and gets placed per prompt, with the same hash and feature and different offsets.

## Accuracy Tests

MMMU-Pro with sgl-eval 0.1.3 and the DeepSeek-V4.1 CI settings from `dsv41_flash_common.py`: 200 examples, 64 threads, `--load-preset-from-model-id deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, thinking on, reasoning effort high), `max_tokens=32768`. Pass 2 reruns the same 200 examples on the same server, so every image hits the cache. Servers and hardware match the speed tests below.

| Server | MMMU-Pro (200) | Truncated | Errors |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | 0.800 | 2.0% | 0 |
| This PR, 4096 MiB, pass 1 (cold) | 0.780 | 3.5% | 0 |
| This PR, 4096 MiB, pass 2 (all hits) | 0.795 | 2.5% | 0 |

All runs clear the CI threshold of 0.75. Standard error at temperature 1.0 and n=200 is about 2.8 points, so the gaps are sampling noise.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Setup:

- 4x NVIDIA B300, TP4 + EP4
- `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, revision `fb2764a5cf321eaa5070ca8f9e892818f477c16d`
- Cookbook B300 High-Throughput flags: `--tp 4 --ep-size 4 --max-running-requests 256 --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto`
- Image `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-dsv41` (torch 2.13.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.6.18). "Before" is its stock processor. "This PR" applies this diff to the same image. The image predates the `patchify_image`/`preprocess_backend` renames on main, so the diff was applied under the old names.
- PIL patchify on both sides. The image does not bundle the Rust image extension.
- Median of 3 runs per cell. Each run uses new images, so turn 0 always misses.

**Multi-turn, images resent every turn.** Same workload as Kimi-K3 in #34411: 32 conversations x 8 turns, concurrency 32, 4 seeded random JPEGs per conversation (512^2 to 2048^2) in the first user message and resent with the full history each turn, 16 output tokens with `ignore_eos`.

| Metric | Before | Cache 256 MiB (default) | Cache 4096 MiB |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Output tok/s | 97.90 | 117.38 (+19.9%) | 125.35 (+28.0%) |
| Requests/s | 6.12 | 7.34 (+19.9%) | 7.83 (+27.9%) |
| Median TTFT, turns 1-7 | 3111 ms | 2300 ms (-26.1%) | 2090 ms (-32.8%) |
| P90 TTFT, turns 1-7 | 4128 ms | 3212 ms (-22.2%) | 2909 ms (-29.5%) |
| Median E2E, turns 1-7 | 4285 ms | 3127 ms (-27.0%) | 2909 ms (-32.1%) |
| Median TTFT, turn 0 (miss) | 9351 ms | 8297 ms | 8390 ms |

Cached patches for a large image are about 20 MB of bf16. The 256 MiB default fits roughly a dozen images per tokenizer worker, so this workload (128 live images) only partially hits. Size the cache to your image working set if you resend many images.

**Unique images, no reuse.** Checks the cold path: 128 single-turn requests with 4 new images each, concurrency 32.

| Metric | Before | Cache 256 MiB (default) | Cache 4096 MiB |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Output tok/s | 44.38 | 46.49 (+4.8%) | 46.28 (+4.3%) |
| Median TTFT | 8070 ms | 7883 ms | 7675 ms |
| P90 TTFT | 11087 ms | 10533 ms | 10650 ms |
| Median E2E | 11478 ms | 10916 ms | 10849 ms |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+"""Unit tests for the DeepSeek-V4.1 image processor."""
+
+import asyncio
+import io
+import unittest
+from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, Mock, patch
+
+import torch
+from PIL import Image
+
+from sglang.srt.multimodal.cache import MultimodalPreprocessCache
+from sglang.srt.multimodal.deepseek_v41_image_processing import patchify_image
+from sglang.srt.multimodal.processors.deepseek_v41 import DeepseekV41ImageProcessor
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+IMAGE_TOKEN_ID = 9
+HF_CONFIG = SimpleNamespace(
+    vision_patch_size=14,
+    vision_downsample_ratio=3,
+    vision_max_n_token=1024,
+    vision_min_pixels=0,
+    vision_max_wh_ratio=None,
+)
+
+
+def _png(width, height):
+    buffer = io.BytesIO()
+    Image.new("RGB", (width, height), (40, 90, 160)).save(buffer, format="PNG")
+    return buffer.getvalue()
+
+
+def _request():
+    return SimpleNamespace(mm_content_hashes=None)
+
+
+class TestDeepseekV41Processor(CustomTestCase):
+    def _make_processor(self):
+        processor = object.__new__(DeepseekV41ImageProcessor)
+        processor.hf_config = HF_CONFIG
+        processor.image_token_id = IMAGE_TOKEN_ID
+        processor.mm_tokens = None
+        processor.preprocess_backend = "cpu"
+        processor.cpu_patchify = Mock(wraps=patchify_image)
+        processor.mm_feature_transport = "cpu"
+        processor.use_cuda_ipc = False
+        processor.processor_fingerprint = "processor"
+        processor.trust_mm_content_hashes = False
+        processor.mm_preprocess_cache = MultimodalPreprocessCache(64 * 1024 * 1024)
+        processor.mm_processor_executor = None
+        processor.io_executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)
+        self.addCleanup(processor.io_executor.shutdown)
+        return processor
+
+    def test_cached_path_composes_the_same_request_as_uncached(self):
+        """A preprocess-cache request must match the legacy path item for item."""
+        images = [_png(84, 84), _png(126, 84)]
+        ids = [1, IMAGE_TOKEN_ID, 2, IMAGE_TOKEN_ID, 3]
+        processor = self._make_processor()
+        decoded = SimpleNamespace(images=[Image.open(io.BytesIO(i)) for i in images])
+        cached = asyncio.run(processor.process_mm_data_async(images, ids, _request()))
+        with patch.object(processor, "load_mm_data", AsyncMock(return_value=decoded)):
+            uncached = asyncio.run(
+                processor._process_mm_data_uncached(images, ids, _request())
+            )
+
+        self.assertEqual(cached.input_ids, uncached.input_ids)
+        self.assertEqual(len(cached.mm_items), 2)
+        for cached_item, uncached_item in zip(cached.mm_items, uncached.mm_items):
+            self.assertEqual(cached_item.offsets, uncached_item.offsets)
+            self.assertEqual(
+                cached_item.model_specific_data, uncached_item.model_specific_data
+            )
+            torch.testing.assert_close(cached_item.feature, uncached_item.feature)
+
+    def test_repeated_image_skips_patchify_and_is_placed_per_prompt(self):
+        """A cache hit reuses the patches and re-places them in the new prompt."""
+        image = _png(84, 84)
+        processor = self._make_processor()
+        first = asyncio.run(
+            processor.process_mm_data_async([image], [1, IMAGE_TOKEN_ID, 2], _request())
+        )
+        second = asyncio.run(
+            processor.process_mm_data_async(
+                [image], [3, 4, 5, IMAGE_TOKEN_ID], _request()
+            )
+        )
+
+        self.assertEqual(processor.cpu_patchify.call_count, 1)
+        first_start, first_end = first.mm_items[0].offsets[0]
+        second_start, second_end = second.mm_items[0].offsets[0]
+        self.assertEqual((first_start, second_start), (1, 3))
+        self.assertEqual(first_end - first_start, second_end - second_start)
+        self.assertEqual(first.mm_items[0].hash, second.mm_items[0].hash)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            first.mm_items[0].feature, second.mm_items[0].feature
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
